source: wcpa_pipeline_colab.ipynb §1, §5-§8; shade bands from the WCPA 'Shade Classification Score' slide (2026-09-28)

person.note: [KARANGAN] in the notebook. Anchored around the Indonesian average V 5.85; to be calibrated from cube_readings.csv + analyst labels.

shade.note: Bands from the WCPA slide: Value light 7-10 / medium 4-6.5 / deep 1-3.5; Chroma bright-clear 6-9 / muted 3-5.5. Centres are band midpoints (derived). MM chroma centre 5.75 is the midpoint between muted and bright because the slide defines no medium chroma band - confirm with the colourist.
shade.scaleNote: Notebook value (SKALA_SHADE); not re-derived for the new bands.

temperature.note: b* - a* thresholds from the Cocory report.

foundationBands.note: L* bands from the Cocory report; first band whose lower bound L* exceeds wins.

complementary.note: [INTERPRETASI] closest reading of the brief; confirm with the colourist before showing to consumers.

recommendation.note: Notebook export keeps the first 10 non-outside shades per category.
recommendation.categoriesNote: Categories the quadrant rules rate. The notebook rated every category, including black mascara and eyeliner and brown brow products, where a skin quadrant says nothing about fit; those are offered unrated in the try-on catalog. Empty list = rate every category (notebook behaviour).

skinMatch.note: Categories whose shades should match the skin (foundation); their recommendations carry skinDeltaE00 (CIEDE2000, shade vs measured skin) and its perceptibility band. Other categories (lip, blush, ...) are meant to differ from skin, so a difference there means nothing. Empty list = report for none. maxDeltaE00 is the brand's match tolerance (policy); null reports the difference with no withinTolerance verdict. The bands themselves (1.0 / 2.0 / 5.0) are fixed in code (domain/perceptibility.go).

retake.note: Worker QC codes (qualityFailed) that mean the photo should be retaken: the illumination ones (too dark, too bright/clipped, mixed light). The codes are the colour worker's vocabulary (worker_colour/wcpa/cells/pipeline_03.py); a code the worker never emits is harmless. /analyze reports retake {required, reasons, provisional}; provisional stays true while the worker's thresholds are [KARANGAN]. enforce=false returns the result with retake filled (the UI decides); enforce=true refuses with 422 retake_required and no shade result.

flags.note: Notebook §5: L* range across face sites above this is flagged.

hueNames.note: Names are the ISCC-NBS colour-name blocks (Kelly 1958, NBS RP2911), level 3, by nearest centroid under CIEDE2000; the table is in code (internal/colour/domain/isccnbs). They replaced the brief's hue-angle families (Beige ... Brown), which named saturated reds 'Peach'.
hueNames.categoriesNote: Unchanged from the brief-era setting: lip, cheek and skin colours get a name, eye products none (the old hue-angle families mislabelled them, e.g. black mascara 'Red'). ISCC-NBS names blacks and browns correctly, so adding eye categories is now a choice, not a fix. Empty list = every category.

presentation.note: Quadrant display names wait for the brand; the season table is a first draft to be reviewed by a colourist.
